method: Five frames sampled at 1s/5s/9s/13s/17s, downscaled to 200px wide, 113,000 pixels analysed. Darkest and lightest deciles averaged; accent isolated as green-dominant saturated pixels.
why_this_exists: CHEAP_PRODUCTION_ECONOMICS_V1 says the premium anchor is the style REFERENCE the cheap tiers are graded against. That was documented and not executed: plates were generated independently of the anchor. These are the anchor's actual values, so cheap tiers can be graded to it IN THE PROMPT rather than colour-corrected afterwards.
findings: THE ANCHOR IS A LIGHT FRAME. Mean luminance 161.9 of 255. Grading plates to a near-black ground would NOT match it - they would read as a different piece cut in beside it.

THE BRAND ACCENT DOES NOT APPEAR AS SPECIFIED. BRAND.md's #7cfc00 renders as #7fb449 in this take's lighting: darker, less saturated, olive rather than chartreuse. Grade cheap tiers to the APPEARANCE (#7fb449), not to the spec (#7cfc00), or they will clash with the very asset they are supposed to match.
THE ACCENT IS 1.31% OF FRAME AREA. It is a trim detail on the presenter's jacket, not a field of colour. A plate flooded with lime would overpower the anchor rather than match it.
The 'paper' palette already chosen for this drop is therefore correct, and correct by luck rather than by measurement - it was argued from the subject before anyone measured the take.

grading_directives_for_cheap_tiers.ground: Light, warm-neutral. Target mean luminance 150-175, not a dark ground.
grading_directives_for_cheap_tiers.accent_usage: A single small accent incident occupying roughly 1-2% of the frame. Never a lime field, never a lime gradient.
grading_directives_for_cheap_tiers.accent_value: #7fb449 as rendered. Reserve #7cfc00 for vector/type where the value is literal and unlit.
grading_directives_for_cheap_tiers.prompt_fragment: warm neutral daylight interior, soft diffuse light, near-white walls, muted mauve-grey shadows, one small olive-green accent object occupying a tiny fraction of frame, 50mm, eye-level, shallow depth of field, real material wear, no text of any kind, deliberate empty area for typography

boundaries: Measured from ONE take. A second take under different lighting will move these values; re-measure rather than assuming.
This describes how the anchor LOOKS. It is not a brand specification and does not override BRAND.md or Design DNA v1 for surfaces that are not being matched to this take.
